# ==============================================================================
# 1. SETUP AND PATHS
# ==============================================================================

```{r}
# Set the base path to one leve up from the current path
current_path <- dirname(getwd())

# Set the state abbreviation
state_abb <- "WV"

print(paste("Current Path:", current_path))
```

# ==============================================================================
# 2. LOAD DATA
# ==============================================================================

```{r}
# Load SVI TDA Data
tda_path <- file.path(current_path, "data", "processed_data", paste0("tda_summaries_2018_", state_abb, "_down.csv"))
svi_tda_data <- read_csv(tda_path, col_types = cols(STCNTY = col_character()))

# Load SMR Data
smr_path <- file.path(current_path, "data", "processed_data", paste0("smr_data_2018_", state_abb, ".csv"))
smr_data <- read_csv(smr_path, col_types = cols(FIPS = col_character()))

# Load Geometry Data (GDB)
geo_path <- file.path(current_path, "data", "raw_data", "SVI2018_US_county.gdb")
# Note: "layers" in GDB might vary, usually it's the main layer name. 
# You can check layers with: st_layers(geo_path)
geo_data <- st_read(geo_path, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  select(FIPS, ST_ABBR) # Select only relevant columns to match your code
```
# ==============================================================================
# 3. DATA MERGING AND PROCESSING
# ==============================================================================
```{r}
# Merge SMR and TDA data (Left join on FIPS = STCNTY)
combined_data <- smr_data %>%
  left_join(svi_tda_data, by = c("FIPS" = "STCNTY"))

# Merge with Geometry (Left join on FIPS)
# Ensure we convert combined_data to an sf object
combined_data <- geo_data %>%
  right_join(combined_data, by = "FIPS") %>%
  filter(ST_ABBR == state_abb)

# Check shape
print(paste("Shape after adding AL column:", nrow(combined_data), ncol(combined_data)))

```
```{r}
# Cleaning the processed data

# remove rows with zero observed deaths (removing missing data)
combined_data <- combined_data %>%
  filter(observed_deaths > 0)


# identify islands (no neighbors) and remove them
nb <- poly2nb(combined_data, row.names = combined_data$FIPS)
islands <- which(card(nb) == 0)
if (length(islands) > 0) { 
  combined_data <- combined_data[-islands, ]
}

# drop rows FIPS starts with ('72', '78', '02', '15', '60')
combined_data <- combined_data %>%
  filter(!substr(FIPS, 1, 2) %in% c('72', '78', '02', '15', '60'))


print(paste("Shape after cleaning:", nrow(combined_data)))

```
# ==============================================================================
# 3.5 PROCESSING DATA FOR THE BYM-T MODEL
# ==============================================================================

```{r}
# aggregate row wise data in the columns that ends with '_AL' and store in a column named 'AL'
combined_data <- combined_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(AL = sum(c_across(ends_with("_AL")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# print the shape after adding AL column
print(paste("Shape after adding AL column:", nrow(combined_data), ncol(combined_data)))

# mean standerdize the AL column
combined_data <- combined_data %>%
  mutate(AL = scale(AL))

```
# ==============================================================================
# 4. SPATIAL ADJACENCY MATRIX (GRAPH)
# ==============================================================================

```{r}
# INLA requires a graph object or file to define neighbors.
# This replaces libpysal.weights.Queen

# Create neighbor list (Queen contiguity)
nb <- poly2nb(combined_data, queen = TRUE)

# Convert to INLA graph file
nb2INLA("wv.graph", nb)
g <- inla.read.graph("wv.graph")

# Create a unique ID for the spatial random effect (INLA requires integer indices)
combined_data$ID_spatial <- 1:nrow(combined_data)

# For BYM2 model in INLA
Q <- inla.graph2matrix(g)

n <- nrow(Q)

print(paste("Number of areas (n):", n))

QQ =inla.scale.model(Q, constr = list(A = matrix(1,1,n), e = 0))

```




```{r}
# INLA requires a graph object or file to define neighbors.
# This replaces libpysal.weights.Queen

# Create neighbor list (Queen contiguity)
nb <- poly2nb(combined_data, queen = TRUE)

# Convert to INLA graph file
nb2INLA("wv.graph", nb)
g <- inla.read.graph("wv.graph")

# Create a unique ID for the spatial random effect (INLA requires integer indices)
combined_data$ID_spatial <- 1:nrow(combined_data)

# For BYM2 model in INLA
Q <- inla.graph2matrix(g)
D <- diag(rowSums(Q))
Q_struct <- D - Q

# Add small jitter
n <- nrow(Q_struct)
Q_perturbed <- Q_struct + diag(rep(max(diag(Q_struct)) * sqrt(.Machine$double.eps), n))

# Compute generalized inverse
Q_inv <- MASS::ginv(as.matrix(Q_perturbed))

# BYM2 scaling factor (geometric mean of diagonal)
scaling_factor_bym2 <- exp(mean(log(diag(Q_inv))))

print(paste("Scaling factor", scaling_factor_bym2))
```

```{r}

get_python_scaling_factor <- function(Q) {
  # Ensure Q is a sparse matrix (dsCMatrix or similar)
  # Q should be the structure matrix (diagonal = # neighbors, off-diag = -1)
  
  n <- nrow(Q)
  
  # 1. Add small jitter (Exactly as in the Python code)
  # np.sqrt(np.finfo(np.float64).eps) is approx sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) in R
  epsilon <- max(diag(Q)) * sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)
  
  # Q_perturbed = Q + epsilon * I
  Q_pert <- Q + Diagonal(n) * epsilon
  
  # 2. Compute the inverse (Sigma)
  # In Python: spsolve(Q_perturbed, Identity)
  # For N=53, a dense solve is fast and accurate
  Sigma <- solve(Q_pert) 
  
  # 3. Apply the Constraint Projection (The "Projector" logic from Python)
  # Python: W = Sigma @ A.T  (Where A is vector of ones)
  # This equals the row sums of Sigma
  W <- rowSums(Sigma) 
  
  # Python: solve(A @ W, np.ones(1)) 
  # This equals 1 / sum(W)
  inv_A_W <- 1 / sum(W)
  
  # Python: Q_inv = Sigma - np.outer(W * ..., W.T)
  # We use standard matrix multiplication for outer product
  correction <- (W %*% t(W)) * inv_A_W
  Q_inv <- Sigma - correction
  
  # 4. Compute Geometric Mean of Diagonal
  # Python: np.exp(np.sum(np.log(np.diag(Q_inv))) / n)
  scaling_factor <- exp(mean(log(diag(Q_inv))))
  
  return(scaling_factor)
}

# --- USAGE ---

# Assuming 'Q_mat' is your structure matrix from inla.graph2matrix(g)
s_factor_python <- get_python_scaling_factor(Q_mat)

print(paste("Python-style Scaling Factor:", s_factor_python))

# Create the scaled matrix
Q_scaled <- Q_mat * s_factor_python


```

```{r}
# SCALE THE MATRIX ONCE AND PASS TO Q()

# 1. Create your adjacency matrix (R_structure)
# Assuming 'g' is your inla.graph object or adjacency matrix
R_structure <- inla.graph2matrix(g) 

# 2. Scale the model using the built-in function 
# (This runs the code you pasted above)
# We add a sum-to-zero constraint (constr) which is standard for BYM scaling
scaled_result <- inla.scale.model(R_structure, 
                                  constr = list(A = matrix(1, 1, nrow(R_structure)), e = 0))

# 3. Extract the scaled matrix
R_scaled <- scaled_result$Q

```



# ==============================================================================
# 5. DEFINE CUSTOM BYM-T MODEL
# ==============================================================================

```{r}
# Define the custom BYM-T model
inla.rgeneric.bym_topological <- function(cmd = c("graph", "Q", "mu", "initial", "log.norm.const", "log.prior", "quit"), theta = NULL, args = NULL) {
  
  # Access environment for variables passed in 'define' (like the Graph 'R')
  envir = parent.env(environment())
  
  
  # Helper function to interpret theta parameters
  interpret.theta <- function() {
    # tau_b: precision parameter
    tau_b <- exp(theta[1L])
    
    # Use softmax-like parameterization for alpha1, alpha2, alpha3
    # to ensure they sum to 1 and are all positive
    eta1 <- exp(theta[2L])
    eta2 <- exp(theta[3L])
    eta_sum <- 1 + eta1 + eta2
    
    alpha1 <- eta1 / eta_sum  # unstructured
    alpha2 <- eta2 / eta_sum  # structured
    alpha3 <- 1 / eta_sum      # topological
    
    return(list(
      tau_b = tau_b,
      alpha1 = alpha1,
      alpha2 = alpha2,
      alpha3 = alpha3
    ))
  }
  
  # R is now the PRE-SCALED matrix passed from args
  R <- args$R 
  n <- nrow(R)
  
  graph <- function() {
    # The graph is based on the adjacency structure plus diagonal
    # Return sparse matrix (upper triangular)
    return(Q())
  }
  
  # Precision matrix Q(theta)
  Q <- function() {
    p <- interpret.theta()
    
    # Retrieve pre-calculated matrices from environment
    # Q_struct is the scaled ICAR matrix: scaling_factor * (Diagonal(rowSums(W)) - W)
    
    # 1. Unstructured Part (alpha1) + Topological Part (alpha3)
    # Note: Both are diagonal, so we sum their weights for efficiency
    # Q_iid = tau * (alpha1 + alpha3) * I
    
    # 2. Structured Part (alpha2)
    # Q_besag = tau * alpha2 * Q_struct
    
    # Combine:
    # We use the pre-calculated 'I_n' and 'Q_struct' from environment
    Q_val <- p$tau_b * ( (p$alpha1 + p$alpha3) * I_n + p$alpha2 * Q_struct )
    return(inla.as.sparse(Q_val))
    
  }
  
  
  # Mean function
  mu <- function() {
    p <- interpret.theta()
    
    # The topological component s_i enters as a mean shift
    # mu_i = (1/sqrt(tau_b)) * sqrt(alpha3) * s_i
    mean_vec <- sqrt(p$alpha3 / p$tau_b) * s_topo
    
    return(mean_vec)
  }
  
  # Log normalizing constant
  log.norm.const <- function() {
    # Let INLA compute it from the Cholesky factorization
    return(numeric(0))
  }
  
  # Log prior
  log.prior <- function() {
    p <- interpret.theta()
    
    # Prior for tau_b: Gamma(a_tau, b_tau) with Jacobian
    # Default: Gamma(1, 0.01) - weakly informative
    log_prior_tau <- dgamma(p$tau_b, shape = prior_tau_a, rate = prior_tau_b, 
                            log = TRUE) + theta[1L]
    
    # Priors for alpha parameters through eta parameterization
    # Use normal priors on theta[2] and theta[3]
    log_prior_alpha1 <- dnorm(theta[2L], mean = 0, sd = prior_alpha_sd, log = TRUE)
    log_prior_alpha2 <- dnorm(theta[3L], mean = 0, sd = prior_alpha_sd, log = TRUE)
    
    val <- log_prior_tau + log_prior_alpha1 + log_prior_alpha2
    
    return(val)
  }
  
  # Initial values
  initial <- function() {
    # tau_b: start with log(precision) = 4 (high precision)
    # alphas: start with equal weights (theta[2]=theta[3]=0 gives approx equal split)
    return(c(4, 0, 0))
  }
  
  # Quit function
  quit <- function() {
    return(invisible())
  }
  
  # Ensure theta is always defined
  if (!length(theta)) theta <- initial()
  
  # Execute the requested command
  val <- do.call(match.arg(cmd), args = list())
  return(val)
  
  # sometimes this is useful, as argument 'graph' and 'quit' 
  # will pass theta=numeric(0) (or NULL in R-3.6...) as 
  # the values of theta are NOT 
  # required for defining the graph. however, this statement 
  # will ensure that theta is always defined. 
  

}


```


```{r}
# --- 2. The Wrapper Function (CRITICAL MISSING PIECE) ---

define.bymt.model <- function(W, s_topo, prior_tau = c(1, 0.01), prior_alpha_sd = 10) {
  
  # A. Pre-calculate dimensions and Identity matrix
  n <- nrow(W)
  I_n <- Matrix::Diagonal(n)
  
  # B. Pre-calculate Scaled ICAR Matrix
  Q_struct =inla.scale.model(W, constr = list(A = matrix(1,1,n), e = 0))
  
  
  # C. Define the rgeneric model
  # We pass all necessary variables into the environment
  model <- inla.rgeneric.define(inla.rgeneric.bym_topological,
                                W = W,
                                s_topo = s_topo,
                                n = n,
                                I_n = I_n,
                                Q_struct = Q_struct,
                                prior_tau_a = prior_tau[1],
                                prior_tau_b = prior_tau[2],
                                prior_alpha_sd = prior_alpha_sd)
  
  return(model)
}

```


```{r}
# 1. Define the model object
bymt_model <- define.bymt.model(W, s_topo)

# 2. Run INLA
# Note: Since this is a latent field model, we use f(..., model=bymt_model)
formula <- Y ~ 1 + f(idx, model = bymt_model)

# Create an index for the random effect
data_df <- data.frame(Y = scotland$data$cases, # or whichever outcome
                      idx = 1:nrow(W))

result <- inla(formula, 
               data = data_df, 
               family = "poisson", # Assuming counts
               E = scotland$data$expected, # Expected counts/offset
               control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE))

summary(result)

```




```{r}

library(spdep)
library(Matrix)
library(SpatialEpi)

# 1. Load Data
data(scotland) # This creates a list named 'scotland'

# 1. Get coordinates of the regions (centroids)
coords <- coordinates(scotland$spatial.polygon)

# 2. Create neighbors based on the 1 nearest neighbor (to ensure no islands)
# Then add more links to make it robust, or just combine approaches.
# A common robust method is 4 nearest neighbors:
k_nb <- knn2nb(knearneigh(coords, k = 4))

# 3. Convert to matrix (Standardized)
W <- nb2mat(k_nb, style = "B")
W <- as(W, "sparseMatrix")

# 3. Prepare covariates
# FIX: Access the data slot inside the list using $data
X <- matrix(scotland$data$AFF, ncol = 1)

# 4. Create topological data (simulation example)
# Simulating a random effect with variance 1
n <- length(scotland$data$AFF)
s_topo <- rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1)

```




```{r}
#5. Define BYM-T model

bymt_model <- define.bymt.model(W, s_topo)
 
# 6. Fit the model
n <- nrow(scotland)

formula <- observed ~ 1 + AFF + f(idx, model = bymt_model)
result <- inla(formula, 
                family = "poisson",
                data = data.frame(
                  observed = scotland$observed,
                  expected = scotland$expected,
                  AFF = scotland$AFF,
                  idx = 1:n
                ),
                E = scotland$expected,
                control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE))
 
# 7. Extract results
summary(result)
```
